title: Naturality of the coherently normalized integral Koszul braiding
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible in every residue field. Use the completed integral constructible category and its completed derived tensor $T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}$ together with the coherently reduction-normalized integral Koszul braiding $\beta^{\mathrm{int}}_{M,N}:T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}(N,M)$ of [def-pod-integral-tensor-constraints]. For arbitrary integral arrows $a:M\to M'$ and $b:N\to N'$, the braiding is natural:
$$\beta^{\mathrm{int}}_{M',N'}\circ T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}(a,b)=T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}(b,a)\circ\beta^{\mathrm{int}}_{M,N}.$$
No finite-field, perfectness, boundedness beyond the constructible integral category, or torsion-freeness hypothesis is added.
